Synthetic municipal tee sheet

Source: R/data.R
sample_tee_sheet.Rd

Simulated reservations for sample_municipal, a fictional 18-hole municipal course. This is not a tee sheet from Dobson Ranch, the Peoria Park District, or Cress Creek Country Club, and it is not an export from foreUP, TeeItUp, GolfNow, or another vendor. The column names are golfops names. Public vendor documents describe tee sheets, check-in, cancellations, and price classes, but this package does not have a verified CSV dictionary for any of those systems, so none of their field names are used here.

Usage

sample_tee_sheet

Format

A golfops_tee_sheet data frame with 735 rows and 14 variables:

course_id

Course identifier. Every row is sample_municipal.

play_date

Date the round is scheduled to start.

tee_time

Scheduled start, "HH:MM", on the 10-minute grid. Weekday starts run from 07:00 through 17:50. Weekend starts run from 06:30 through 18:20.

booking_id

Reservation identifier, B- plus five digits, unique on this sheet and ordered by play date, tee time, and creation.

players_booked

Players on this reservation. An integer from 1 to max_players.

players_checked_in

Players who arrived and paid. Zero unless booking_status is completed. Never above players_booked.

max_players

Player cap for the start, 4 on every row. Do not sum this column.

holes

9 or 18. This does not create a second tee sheet.

booking_status

reserved, completed, cancelled, or no_show.

booking_channel

online, phone, or walk_in. Walk-in reservations are same-day and are not used for play dates after the extract.

rate_type

standard, senior, junior, member, or promotional. Promotional rates are more common after 15:00.

price_per_player

Green fee for one player, in US dollars, from attribute rate_card. It depends on rate_type, weekday or weekend, and holes.

booking_date

Date the reservation was made. On or before play_date, and on or before the extract date.

revenue

Realized green-fee dollars. Missing while reserved. The posted fee on those rows, players_booked * price_per_player, is future booking value and is not stored in this column. Zero when cancelled or no_show. Otherwise players_checked_in * price_per_player.

Attributes synthetic, seed (704), as_of, the operating window, rate_card, and decisions record the simulation. row_grain is reservation.

Source

Synthetic data from data-raw/sample_tee_sheet.R, set.seed(704), RNGkind Mersenne-Twister. No operator file was copied. Documents consulted while choosing the grain, and not used as a column dictionary, include foreUP's tee-sheet print article (https://foreup.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360006796293-Printing-the-Tee-Sheet), its check-in article (https://foreup.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360006726354-Checking-in-a-Tee-Time), and its Tee Times Sales by Price Class article (https://foreup.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/45261809335835-Tee-Times-Sales-By-Price-Class). Those articles confirm individual booked and cancelled tee times, partial check-in, price class, and CSV export of reports. They do not publish the tee-sheet columns. Dobson Ranch's public booking page is TeeItUp (https://dobson-ranch.book.teeitup.com/), which shows open inventory rather than an internal sheet. Cress Creek's tee-sheet vendor was not identified. Peoria Park District minutes for November 8, 2023 record a foreUP license extension (https://peoriaparks.org/wp-content/uploads/11.8.23-Regular-Board-Meeting-Minutes-1.pdf) and do not include an export layout.

Details

One row is one reservation. Two reservations may share a tee time, and their player counts add. A cancelled reservation stays on the sheet and does not hold a player slot, so a later reservation can use that start. max_players is the cap for the start, copied onto every reservation at that start. Summing max_players double-counts a shared start and still misses starts with no reservation. Those empty starts are not rows. Inventory is the operating window: weekday 07:00–18:00 and weekend 06:30–18:30, every 10 minutes, four players per start. The end clock is not itself a start. Pass that window to course_capacity().

The sheet is an end-of-day extract on 2026-06-19. Play dates after that day are reserved or cancelled. Earlier play dates have a terminal status. no_show means nobody in that reservation checked in. completed can still have players_checked_in below players_booked when part of the group played. Nine-hole and 18-hole reservations use the same starting inventory. A nine-hole player still takes one player slot.

Realized revenue is the green fee collected at check-in: players_checked_in * price_per_player. Cancelled and no-show reservations realize zero. There is no no-show fee and no cancellation fee. On a reserved row, players_booked * price_per_player is future booking value. It is not realized revenue. This sheet does not model prepayment, so revenue is missing for those rows. Prices are synthetic dollars per player. They are not a Peoria posted card and not Dobson Ranch revenue divided by rounds. The assumed card is stored in attribute rate_card. Carts, tax, and golfer names are absent.

daily_utilization() asks for date, tee_time, and players, and it has no course id. This sample has one course. Realized player utilization uses players_checked_in on completed rows, and only play dates through the extract, 2026-06-19. slot_utilization is those players divided by player slots. Reservations after the extract have not been played, so checked-in counts are zero there. Evaluate those future bookings with booked utilization: drop cancelled rows and pass players_booked. Groups on the same start count as one occupied tee time. A start whose supplied player counts sum to zero is not occupied.

Examples

data(sample_tee_sheet)
sheet <- sample_tee_sheet
as_of <- attr(sheet, "as_of")
dates <- sort(unique(sheet$play_date[sheet$play_date <= as_of]))
weekend <- as.POSIXlt(dates)$wday %in% c(0L, 6L)
capacity <- course_capacity(
  date = dates,
  window_start = ifelse(
    weekend,
    attr(sheet, "weekend_window_start"),
    attr(sheet, "weekday_window_start")
  ),
  window_end = ifelse(
    weekend,
    attr(sheet, "weekend_window_end"),
    attr(sheet, "weekday_window_end")
  ),
  tee_interval_minutes = attr(sheet, "tee_interval_minutes"),
  players_per_start = attr(sheet, "players_per_start")
)
played <- sheet[
  sheet$booking_status == "completed" & sheet$play_date <= as_of,
]
use <- daily_utilization(
  data.frame(
    date = played$play_date,
    tee_time = played$tee_time,
    players = played$players_checked_in
  ),
  capacity
)
use[, c("date", "players", "player_slots", "slot_utilization")]
